title: Gateway tool unrestricted gatewayUrl SSRF
summary: A tool-supplied gatewayUrl flowed to the Gateway WebSocket client without validation/allowlisting, letting the OpenClaw host attempt outbound connections to caller-chosen targets. The upstream advisory limits the common effect to connection attempts and, where observable, limited reachability probing; it does not establish cloud metadata disclosure.
ai_role: Endor Labs’ case-specific report describes its AI SAST engine’s trace for this finding and the researcher’s subsequent validation with a proof of concept. This supports AI-assisted discovery with human validation; the specific model is not named. The six-case article was updated after initial publication, so the exact first public date of its current attribution text is not established.
classification_note: The upstream security advisory documents the public disclosure and fix. The sources do not establish whether defenders knew of the issue or whether it was exploited before disclosure.
remediation_note: 2026.2.14 and later are listed as patched. The fix restricts gatewayUrl to configured loopback/remote gateway locations and rejects disallowed protocol, credentials, query/hash and non-root paths.

impacts.conditions: Gateway / Canvas / Cron tool invocation with an attacker-controlled gatewayUrl; external access is not drive-by unless the deployment exposes tool calls to untrusted users.
impacts.exploitation: The sources report validation or describe attack conditions but do not report observed exploitation.
